articles.title: Jordan gets $6.7bn funding for water desalination project
articles.summary:
Jordan gets $6.7bn funding for water desalination project

A desalination project in water-poor Jordan has drawn investment of $6.7 bn and talks are underway to launch similar projects in Syria and Yemen, the head of the UN's Green Climate Fund told Reuters on Wednesday.

The project is the biggest commitment yet by the world's largest multilateral climate fund. It aims to address water stress at a time when the climate crisis is increasing the problem.

Jordan ranks among the countries with the least available water.

Launched officially on Wednesday by Prince Faisal bin Al Hussein, the younger brother of Jordan's King Abdullah II, the Aqaba–Amman Water Desalination and Conveyance Project will eventually move 300 million cubic metres of additional water and serve 40 percent of the population.

Last year, the fund approved $295m in grants and loans that attracted further public and private sector funding to reach a total of $6.7bn.

The Green Climate Fund was set up under the United Nations climate framework to help developing nations adapt and curb their emissions.

articles.title: Exclusive: Labour MPs quit Somaliland group over Israel and chair’s ties to far-right Restore
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Labour MPs quit Somaliland group over Israel and chair’s ties to far-right Restore

Submitted by Daniel Tester on Tue, 11/17/2026 - 14:31
Kim Johnson and Abtisam Mohamed say they disagree with APPG's direction after Israeli official was invited to parliamentary event
A picture posted by British MP Gavin Williamson (L) of his January 2025 meeting Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, better known as Irro [Facebook]
Off

Kim Johnson, an MP from the UK’s Labour Party, was helping to host an event in the UK parliament marking the anniversary of Somaliland’s self-declared independence when she was told that an official from another government was on their way to attend.

“When I heard there would be an Israeli government official there, I just left the event as quickly as I could,” Johnson told Middle East Eye.

The unexpected appearance of an Israeli official at the May event was the final straw for Johnson, a backbencher on Labour’s left and an advocate for Palestinian rights, who quit the UK’s all-party parliamentary group (APPG) on Somaliland soon after.

Abtisam Mohamed, the Labour MP for Sheffield Central and Johnson’s deputy in the group, also resigned her post this week, Middle East Eye can reveal, while Kerry McCarthy, Labour MP for Bristol East, has stopped participating in the group’s activities until its chair, the Conservative MP Gavin Williamson, resigns.

MEE understands that the APPG, Westminster’s main forum advocating for Somaliland and its diaspora, has not met since before the UK parliament’s summer recess amid fallout over Israel's recognition of Somaliland and Williamson's ties to the hardline anti-immigration party Restore Britain.

Mohamed, who sits on the UK parliament's Foreign Affairs committee, told MEE that she will "continue to support the aspirations of the Somaliland people" but had quit due to "long-term differences over the direction the APPG is taking".

Johnson, whose Liverpool constituency contains a large Somaliland diaspora population, had been a member of the group for more than six years, and served as its co-chair alongside Williamson until her resignation.

She told MEE that the group’s “whole ethos changed” after Israel became the only state to recognise the breakaway territory from Somalia in December.

“I still of course support my local community, and will do so on independence days,” she said.

“But the Israeli recognition has caused such division within communities that you now even have cases of pro-Palestine people being attacked for their views.”

APPG leaders' Restore and UAE ties

The APPG’s leadership spanned a wide cross-section of the UK political spectrum, with Johnson, Mohamed and McCarthy sitting alongside Williamson, who served as an advisor to Restore Britain, and Edward Udny-Lister, the Tory peer who was once Boris Johnson’s chief of staff, and now heads the Abu Dhabi arm of the emerging markets investor Gemcorp, long criticised for its historic ties to Russia.

In June 2025, the group published a report authored by Williamson, a former defence minister, touting Somaliland's "vast untapped reserves of oil, gas and rare earths" and arguing that recognition could help the UK develop a military base in the strategic port of Berbera, among other benefits.

Somalia's president accuses UAE of 'interference' in the country
Read More »

Williamson's office, which adminsters the APPG as its secretariat, said it had no role in inviting the Israeli official to the parliamentary event, and understood that the official had been invited by Somaliland's UK mission.

Israel’s courting of Somaliland has made the territory a more contentious geopolitical flashpoint than ever. 

Since Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar visited Somaliland's capital Hargeisa in January, Israel has begun training Somaliland’s army, with the breakaway state taking the highly controversial step of establishing an embassy in Jerusalem in June.

In return for recognition, Somaliland officials have floated the prospect of allowing Israel to build a military base on the territory – a move that would help Israel boost its influence in the Horn of Africa within striking range of Yemen’s Houthis.

Hargeisa has also developed strong ties with the UAE, which has built port infrastructure and military bases in the territory.

The UAE was lauded in the APPG's report as having "wasted no time in capitalising on Berbera’s potential" in its "strategy to counterbalance Iranian influence and deter further Houthi aggression". 

Somalia's president, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, accused the UAE of "interference" in his country's internal affairs on Tuesday amid mounting tensions between Abu Dhabi and Mogadishu.

Rupert Lowe ties

Beside the group’s links to Israel, Johnson and McCarthy told MEE that they also had concerns about Williamson’s support for anti-immigration politicians in the UK.

In June, Williamson signed a letter penned by Restore Britain leader Rupert Lowe calling for the mass deportation of refugees brought to the UK via safe and legal routes.

The letter states: “Put simply - we do not want these people in our country.”  

McCarthy, who co-founded the APPG in 2005, called Williamson’s signing of the letter a “betrayal” of Somaliland’s UK community.

“I don’t believe you can support Somaliland without supporting its people, wherever they may live,” she said, adding that many of the Somalilanders in her constituency originally came to the UK as refugees, fleeing the Somali government's persecution of the Isaaq clan in the 1980s in what was widely described as a genocide.

The chairman of the #Somaliland Independence Recognition Institution, @GavinWilliamson - full speech from last week’s launch event in Hargeisa. https://t.co/idQEJFtq4w

— Somalilanders (@Somaalilanders) May 26, 2026

Williamson has become one of Somaliland’s most dedicated international advocates since he was relegated to Westminster’s backbenches in 2022 after a series of gaffes and scandals in ministerial posts.

Despite his support for nativist politics in the UK, he has travelled extensively to Hargeisa, and has been given honorary Somaliland citizenship in return for his advocacy.

Williamson did not attend the independence day event in the UK parliament because he was in Hargeisa mingling with Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, better known as Irro, for the launch of a new body lobbying for Somaliland's independence.

In speeches to crowds in Hargeisa that day, he declared: “I am deeply privileged to be able to call myself a Somalilander”, and called the breakaway nation “a beacon for what every nation aspires to be”, while draped in Somaliland’s flag.

Williamson, who also chairs a private membership organisation seeking to boost British commercial ties to Africa, declined MEE’s request for comment. 

The Somaliland mission and the Israeli embassy to the UK did not respond to MEE's requests for comment.

articles.title: How the Houthi advance on Aden exposes Saudi Arabia's strategic trap
articles.summary:
How the Houthi advance on Aden exposes Saudi Arabia's strategic trap

Submitted by Shady Ibrahim on Tue, 11/17/2026 - 16:00
Riyadh faces a complex dilemma: protecting its Yemeni allies and shielding its own economy have become increasingly difficult to reconcile
Armoured vehicles are left by the sea as Saudi-backed forces sustain losses against Yemen’s Houthis, in this screengrab from 16 November 2026 (Ansar Allah Military Media/Handout via Reuters)
Off

The forces that were supposed to recover Yemen’s western coast are now concentrating on defending Aden. That reversal captures the scale of Saudi Arabia’s predicament.

Southern forces fighting alongside Yemen’s internationally recognised government this week announced their withdrawal from positions around Bab al-Mandab and Dhubab. Their stated priority was to secure Aden and neighbouring governorates.

A six-week counteroffensive had failed to reverse the Houthis’ coastal gains, as the government’s political centre took precedence over the maritime corridor its supporters had sought to recover.

Meanwhile, military and government sources told the AFP news agency that Houthi fighters had reached positions approximately 60 kilometres from Aden.

The city’s fall is neither established nor inevitable. But the threat already produces consequences: it changes where government forces deploy, what Saudi Arabia must defend, and the terms on which the next round of negotiations could begin.

The current offensive connects battles that might appear separate on a map. The Houthis advanced roughly 150 kilometres along the Red Sea coast in a week in September, capturing Mokha and reaching Bab al-Mandab. The element of surprise, and relatively centralised command, helped them exploit divisions among their opponents.

Progress became harder as fighting moved towards the Taiz-Lahij highlands, where local resistance strengthened and the terrain complicated further advances.

The pressure towards Aden nevertheless gave the coastal campaign a second political life. Threatening the government’s temporary capital pushed its opponents to reconsider whether they could afford to remain around the strait.

Shifting the balance

That pressure on government supply lines reportedly contributed to the withdrawal. The broader significance is that the Houthis can gain from an offensive before achieving their ultimate objective: forcing opponents to abandon another priority can itself alter the balance.

This does not amount to uncontested Houthi command of Bab al-Mandab. Territorial influence along its shores increases maritime leverage, but it does not automatically establish control over every approach, nor does it ensure the ability to close international navigation. Rather, it gives the Houthis the upper hand to control who can cross Bab al-Mandab.

Aden has experienced Houthi occupation before. In 2015, the movement advanced alongside military units loyal to former president Ali Abdullah Saleh. They entered the city and controlled substantial areas before being expelled in July by a diverse local resistance supported by the Saudi-led coalition.

Each new advance makes that settlement more urgent, while giving the strongest armed actor additional reasons to demand more for accepting it

That history matters because it challenges two assumptions: that Houthi entry would necessarily produce durable control, and that southern resistance constitutes a unified political force.

The coalition that fought them included southern activists, independents, Salafis and Islah supporters. Shared opposition to the Houthis did not erase competing visions of Yemen’s future.

Today, Aden’s military strength remains difficult to quantify. There is no independently verified public count of fighters presently available to defend it.

A March 2025 British government country assessment, citing data from the conflict monitor Acled, estimated that there were approximately 15,000 Security Belt personnel across Aden, Lahij, Abyan and al-Dhale combined. That figure cannot credibly be presented as the city’s current defending force. Administrative strength, personnel actually present, and troops capable of sustained combat are different measures.

The Sanaa Center’s review of early 2026 describes Saudi-led security restructuring involving the Giants Brigades, Nation’s Shield forces and local security bodies. Reorganising institutions, however, does not instantly produce common loyalties or effective coordination.

Limits of tribal arithmetic

Nor can Aden’s defence be reduced to a tribal headcount. The city has a diverse urban society, while important military networks draw recruits and commanders from its surrounding governorates.

The Subayha tribe played a significant role in resisting Houthi-Saleh forces in 2015, viewing their advance as an intrusion into local territory. The Yafa tribe has supplied substantial recruitment networks for southern security formations, while Dhale and Radfan are important regional bases for southern mobilisation.

These connections can sustain resistance through local legitimacy, social obligations and memories of earlier fighting. They can also reproduce rivalries over command, resources and representation.

A community’s opposition to the Houthis does not establish unconditional loyalty to every commander claiming to defend it. Saudi Arabia thus faces a political problem embedded within a military one. Equipment and salaries can sustain formations; they cannot alone settle who commands them, or whose authority they recognise.

For Riyadh, the danger extends beyond another setback for a Yemeni ally. Pressure on Aden coincides with threats to Saudi aviation, energy infrastructure and shipping. The kingdom must consider both the survival of its partners, and the economic consequences of continuing confrontation.

Disruption around Hormuz makes alternative export infrastructure towards the Red Sea more valuable. Insecurity around Bab al-Mandab exposes the limits of treating those alternatives as insulated from the regional conflict.

The resulting dilemma is severe. A greater Saudi military commitment could help prevent further government losses, while inviting additional attacks. Accommodation could reduce immediate economic pressure, while consolidating a stronger Houthi position. Neither choice offers a reliable exit.

The relationship between land and sea also explains why maritime protection alone cannot resolve the crisis. Naval deployments may protect individual vessels; they cannot settle the struggle over authority ashore, which repeatedly generates threats to navigation.

For Egypt, prolonged insecurity threatens confidence in the Suez route. For European and Asian economies, it sustains uncertainty over transport and energy. Their interests favour stability, but their willingness to assume the costs of producing it remains uneven.

War and bargaining

The timing adds another layer. A third American aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East, expanding Washington’s military options as renewed attacks on Iran remain under consideration.

Military availability does not prove a decision to attack. US President Donald Trump faces divisions within his administration, with Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly favouring negotiations, and Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth advocating further military action. Blockade and sanctions present another option. 

Alongside public anger over rising prices and mounting congressional pressure, these disagreements leave Saudi Arabia dependent on an ally with overwhelming military power but an unsettled strategy for ending the war. 

Saudi-Yemen conflict: The notion of an 'American saviour' is dead
Read More »

Equally, domestic political weakness does not guarantee restraint. Leaders under pressure may avoid escalation or seek a limited operation they believe can restore credibility.

Following the Republican midterm defeat, Democrats are preparing to control both congressional chambers in January. That could strengthen scrutiny and funding constraints, but it does not automatically remove the president’s capacity to use force.

If major strikes resume, Tehran could seek to combine military resistance with negotiations under fire, using regional disruption to raise the price of American objectives. Whether that produces concessions would depend on Iran’s own resilience, the damage it suffers, and the response of neighbouring states.

The Houthi advance potentially strengthens that bargaining environment.

Meanwhile, civilians bear the consequences. The UN has warned that restrictions on supplies into Taiz threaten hospitals, water provision, and access to essential goods. Saudi air strikes are causing destruction and have sparked further displacement of civilians. This suffering is already occurring, regardless of whether Aden falls.

For Saudi Arabia, the question is how to protect its security when the political order it supports remains fragmented.

Aden exposes the difficulty of seeking a secure border, reliable allies, and protected trade routes without a viable Yemeni settlement. Each new advance makes that settlement more urgent, while giving the strongest armed actor additional reasons to demand more for accepting it.

Somalia's president accuses UAE of 'interference' in his country

The president of Somalia has accused the United Arab Emirates of "interference" in his country's internal affairs.

Speaking in a televised address, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud said the UAE had established a military presence, including bases, outside Mogadishu’s national security framework without the government's approval.

He said the country had also funded armed groups and opponents of the central government.

"Somalia is not a thoroughfare to be traversed illegally - it is not a commodity to be bought, nor is it a place that one can enter or leave at will," Hassan Sheikh said.

Tensions between the UAE and Somalia have been high for many years, in part due to the former's support for the breakaway nation of Somaliland.

The Department for Transport opened a consultation this week on a proposed greenhouse gas intensity standard, which the government expects to introduce from 2030. The regime would …

articles.title: Smaller Tankers Join Hormuz Shuttle Trade to Keep Oil Flowing
articles.summary: Oil is increasingly moving through the Strait of Hormuz on smaller vessels, helping sustain exports as attacks on supertankers squeeze availability of the ships that typically dominate the trade.

articles.title: UAE’s ADNOC L&S Says One Crew Member Missing After Attack on Its Vessel in Hormuz
articles.summary: The United Arab Emirates' ADNOC L&S said on Wednesday that one crew member was missing and 11 injured after one of its vessels was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday.

articles.title: U.S. Military Strikes Iranian Missile Site Near Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: By Arsalan Shahla and Jen Judson (Bloomberg) — American warplanes hit an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Persian Gulf on Tuesday, a US military official said,...

articles.title: Gulf Oil Flow at Risk From Lack of Empty Tankers, Tracker Says
articles.summary: The number of empty tankers sailing to collect cargoes of Middle East crude is sliding, a trend that could jeopardize the recent revival in the region’s oil flows to global markets, according to Tankertrackers.com, a firm that monitors vessel movements.

articles.title: Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington
articles.summary: Tehran rejects any suggestion it was plotting a so-called dirty bomb attack on the US capital as "baseless".

articles.title: Bahrain court sentences dozens of Shia Muslims to life in prison, activists say
articles.summary:
Most of those jailed on Iran-linked terrorism charges are clerics, a UK-based human rights group, claiming confessions were forced.

Bahraini authorities accused the 69 unnamed defendants of establishing a terrorist group linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards.

articles.title: Houthi rebel advance in Yemen may further destabilise global economy
articles.summary: The Iran-backed Houthis are gaining ground and their advance could have dangerous consequences, writes the BBC's security correspondent.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Blízkého východu zůstává kritická, což dokládají nedávné útoky Houthiů na energetickou infrastrukturu v Saúdské Arábii a přetrvávající napadení tankerů v Hormuzském průlivu. Hrozby odvetných kroků ze strany Íránu a incidenty spojené s kybernetickou bezpečností nadále narušují stabilitu mezinárodního obchodu.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Middle East remains critical, highlighted by recent Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and ongoing strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian retaliation threats and cybersecurity incidents continue to disrupt international trade stability.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat přetrvávající vysokou volatilitu cen komodit a ropy kvůli nezmenšenému napětí v Perském zálivu a útokům na infrastrukturu. Finanční trhy budou extrémně citlivě reagovat na jakékoliv zprávy o vojenské odvetě.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, high volatility in commodity and oil prices is expected to persist due to unabated tensions in the Persian Gulf and infrastructure attacks. Financial markets will remain extremely sensitive to any news regarding military retaliation.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Blízkého východu a námořních tras zůstává kritická, což potvrzují nedávné útoky na energetickou infrastrukturu a ropné tankery v regionu. Houtiové pokračují v útocích, přičemž nejnovější zásahy v saúdském hlavním městě podtrhují přetrvávající rizika pro globální logistiku a dodávky energií.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Middle East and maritime corridors remains critical, underscored by recent attacks on energy infrastructure and oil tankers in the region. The Houthis continue their strikes, with the latest hits in the Saudi capital highlighting persistent risks to global logistics and energy supplies.
archive.forecast_cs: V následujících dnech lze očekávat zvýšenou volatilitu na energetických trzích a pokračující bezpečnostní opatření v námořní dopravě. Jakékoliv nové zprávy o eskalaci v Perském zálivu okamžitě ovlivní ceny ropy.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, heightened volatility in energy markets and ongoing security measures in maritime shipping are expected. Any fresh news of escalation in the Persian Gulf will immediately impact oil prices.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Blízkého východu a Perského zálivu zůstává napjatá kvůli pokračujícím útokům na ropné tankery a vojenská zařízení. Růst hrozeb pro námořní dopravu nadále vynucuje přísná bezpečnostní opatření a prodlužování tras lodí mimo rizikové oblasti.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Middle East and the Persian Gulf remains tense due to ongoing attacks on oil tankers and military installations. Heightened threats to maritime shipping continue to necessitate strict security measures and the rerouting of vessels away from high-risk zones.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat přetrvávající volatilitu na komoditních trzích a opatrnost investorů kvůli rizikům další eskalace v oblasti Perského zálivu.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, persistent volatility in commodity markets and investor caution due to risks of further escalation in the Persian Gulf region are expected.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Blízkého východu a Perského zálivu prudce eskaluje po sérii útoků na námořní dopravu, včetně minového incidentu v Hormuzském průlivu a úderů na vojenská zařízení. Rizika pro komerční plavbu a energetické koridory zůstávají na kritické úrovni.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Middle East and Persian Gulf is escalating sharply following a series of attacks on maritime traffic, including a naval mine incident in the Strait of Hormuz and strikes on military installations. Risks to commercial shipping and energy corridors remain at a critical level.
archive.forecast_cs: V příštích dnech lze očekávat vysokou volatilitu cen ropy a přetrvávající opatrnost investorů kvůli reálnému riziku další ozbrojené eskalace v oblasti Perského zálivu.
archive.forecast_en: High volatility in oil prices and persistent investor caution are expected over the coming days due to the tangible risk of further armed escalation in the Persian Gulf.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Perského zálivu a Hormuzského průlivu zůstává vysoce nestabilní kvůli opakovaným útokům na tankery a námořním minám. Navzdory částečnému oživení exportu ropy přetrvávají přímé hrozby pro globální námořní dopravu a bezpečnost posádek.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz remains highly volatile due to repeated tanker attacks and naval mines. Despite a partial recovery in oil exports, direct threats to global maritime shipping and crew safety persist.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující volatilitu cen komodit a napětí kolem námořních tras v důsledku přetrvávajících vojenských incidentů.
archive.forecast_en: Continued volatility in commodity prices and tension around shipping lanes are expected over the coming days due to ongoing military incidents.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Perského zálivu a Hormuzského průlivu zůstává kritická kvůli pokračujícím útokům na tankery, námořním minám a přímým vojenským incidentům mezi USA a Iránem. Provoz v klíčových námořních trasách je nadále silně narušen, což generuje enormní tlak na globální dodavatelské řetězce.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz remains critical due to ongoing tanker attacks, naval mines, and direct military incidents between the US and Iran. Traffic in key maritime routes continues to be severely disrupted, generating enormous pressure on global supply chains.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat vysokou volatilitu na energetických trzích a přetrvávající bezpečnostní opatření kolem strategických úžin vlivem přímých konfrontací.
archive.forecast_en: High volatility in energy markets and persistent security measures around strategic straits are expected over the coming days due to direct confrontations.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Blízkého východu a Rudého moře zůstává vysoce napjatá kvůli nedávným přímým útokům íránských Revolučních gard (IRGC) na americkou základnu v Bahrajnu a aktivitám Houthiů. Konflikt nadále narušuje námořní trasy, vyvolává obavy z uzavření klíčových úžin a nutí přepravce k prodlužování tras.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Middle East and Red Sea remains highly tense due to recent direct attacks by Iran's IRGC on a US base in Bahrain and Houthi activities. The conflict continues to disrupt maritime routes, raise concerns over the closure of strategic straits, and force shippers to take longer detours.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat zvýšenou volatilitu na energetických trzích a přetrvávající bezpečnostní opatření v oblasti Perského zálivu a Rudého moře kvůli eskalaci útoků. Diplomatické snahy budou pod silným tlakem vzhledem k vojenským odvetným akcím.
archive.forecast_en: High volatility in energy markets and persistent security measures across the Persian Gulf and Red Sea are expected over the coming days due to escalating attacks. Diplomatic efforts will remain under severe pressure amid military retaliations.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Perského zálivu a Blízkého východu eskaluje po přímých útocích na americké vojenské radary a infrastrukturu v Bahrajnu. Námořní doprava čelí hrozbám nejen v Rudém moři, ale nově i v Hormuzském průlivu, kde došlo k zasažení ropného tankeru námořní minou.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Persian Gulf and Middle East has escalated sharply following direct attacks on US military radar and infrastructure in Bahrain. Maritime trade faces severe threats not only in the Red Sea but increasingly in the Strait of Hormuz, where an oil tanker was struck by a naval mine.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující volatilitu na energetických trzích a zvýšené napětí v Perském zálivu i Rudém moři v důsledku eskalujících útoků na vojenskou a námořní infrastrukturu.
archive.forecast_en: Continued volatility in energy markets and elevated tensions in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea are expected over the coming days as attacks on military and maritime infrastructure escalate.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu zůstává kritická kvůli přímým útokům na americké základny v Bahrajnu, minovým incidentům v Hormuzském průlivu a aktivitě Houthiů v oblasti Rudého moře. Přítomnost tří amerických úderných skupin letadlových lodí odráží extrémní stupeň eskalace konfliktu.
archive.security_status_en: The regional security situation remains critical due to direct attacks on US bases in Bahrain, mine incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, and Houthi activity in the Red Sea region. The presence of three US carrier strike groups reflects an extreme level of conflict escalation.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat vysokou nervozitu na energetických trzích a pokračující vojenské manévry v Perském zálivu i Rudém moři. Riziko dalšího přímého střetu zůstává akutní.
archive.forecast_en: High nervousness in energy markets and ongoing military maneuvers in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea are expected over the coming days. The risk of further direct confrontation remains acute.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Rudého moře a Perského zálivu eskaluje po útocích na ropné tankery v Hormuzském průlivu a přímých dronech na americkou základnu v Bahrajnu. Jemnští Hútiové navíc postupují blíže k Adenu v návaznosti na stahování vládních sil z oblasti Bab al-Mandebu.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Red Sea and Persian Gulf is escalating following naval mine strikes on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and drone attacks on a US military base in Bahrain. Furthermore, Houthi forces are pushing closer to Aden following the withdrawal of government troops from the Bab al-Mandeb area.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další testování americké přítomnosti v regionu, vysokou volatilitu cen ropy a přetrvávající bezpečnostní opatření kolem námořních tras.
archive.forecast_en: Further testing of the US regional presence, high volatility in oil prices, and persistent security measures around maritime routes are expected over the coming days.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Blízkého východu a námořních koridorů se nadále vyhsoce eskaluje v důsledku přímých útoků na tankery v Hormuzském průlivu a úderů na americké základny v Bahrajnu. Houtiové mezitím postupují v Jemenu, což ohrožuje klíčový průliv Bab al-Mandab a celkovou svobodu globální plavby navzdory masivnímu nasazení tří amerických letadlových lodí.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Middle East and maritime corridors continues to escalate severely due to direct attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and strikes on US bases in Bahrain. Meanwhile, Houthi forces are advancing in Yemen, threatening the critical Bab al-Mandab strait and overall freedom of global navigation despite the massive deployment of three US aircraft carriers.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat stupňování vojenských operací v oblasti Hormuzského průlivu a Jemenu, což povede k další volatilitě cen ropy a přetrvávajícím bezpečnostním opatřením.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, an escalation of military operations in the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen is expected, leading to further oil price volatility and persistent security measures.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Hormuzského průlivu, Rudého moře a přilehlých vodních cest se dramaticky zostřuje v důsledku útoků na tankery, námořních min a rozsáhlých vojenských operací USA a jejich spojenců. Postup Houthiů v Jemenu a eskalace napětí s Iránem nadále ohrožují klíčové globální námořní trasy a energetickou infrastrukturu.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, and surrounding waterways is sharply deteriorating due to tanker attacks, naval mines, and extensive military operations by the US and its allies. Houthi advances in Yemen and escalating tensions with Iran continue to threaten critical global shipping lanes and energy infrastructure.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další eskalaci vojenských střetů v oblasti Hormuzského průlivu a Jemenu, což udrží ceny energií a volatilitu na vysokých úrovních.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further escalation of military clashes in the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen is expected, keeping energy prices and volatility elevated.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Blízkého východu a Rudého moře zůstává vysoce nestabilní kvůli pokračujícím útokům Houthiů a eskalaci napětí mezi USA a Íránem v Hormuzském průlivu. Zásahy tankerů a útoky na vojenské základny v Perském zálivu nutí loďařské společnosti k dalším obchvatům a udržují logistická rizika na maximu.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Middle East and Red Sea remains highly volatile due to ongoing Houthi attacks and escalating US-Iran tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. Tanker strikes and attacks on military bases in the Persian Gulf are forcing shipping companies to make further detours, keeping logistical risks at a maximum.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující vojenské manévry a asymetrické útoky v oblasti Perského zálivu a Jemenu, které udrží ceny energií a dopravní rizika na zvýšených úrovních.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued military maneuvers and asymmetric attacks in the Persian Gulf and Yemen are expected, keeping energy prices and shipping risks elevated.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Rudého moře a Perského zálivu eskaluje po přímých útocích na tankery (včetně plavidel ADNOC) a vzájemných úderech mezi USA a Íránem. Postup Houthiů v Jemenu a rozšiřování konfliktů na okolní státy nadále ohrožují klíčové námořní koridory.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Red Sea and Persian Gulf is escalating following direct attacks on tankers (including ADNOC vessels) and reciprocal strikes between the US and Iran. The Houthi advance in Yemen and the spillover of conflict into neighboring states continue to threaten critical maritime corridors.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování vojenských úderů a asymetrických akcí v oblasti Perského zálivu a Jemenu, což udrží ceny energií a dopravní rizika na zvýšených úrovních.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued military strikes and asymmetric actions in the Persian Gulf and Yemen are expected, keeping energy prices and shipping risks elevated.
